text: Git is a version control system that helps developers manage changes to their code. One of its most useful features is branching. A branch lets you work on new ideas without affecting the main code. For example, you can create a feature branch to build a new function safely. When your work is finished, you can merge the branch back into the main project. Many teams also use pull requests to review changes before merging. This workflow keeps the code organized, reduces mistakes, and allows several people to work at the same time. Understanding branching is an important step for anyone learning to use Git effectively.
